subject: APAC & EU service disruption — customer reroute steps and postmortem actions
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: samantha.jenkins@acme-analytics.com, mike@cloudops.io
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T01:04:00Z
Subject: APAC & EU service disruption — immediate customer notice

Samantha / Mike,

We're sending a quick update: between 00:40-01:00 UTC we observed escalating connectivity errors in two cloud regions serving APAC (ap-northeast-1) and parts of EU (eu-west-1). This resulted in increased 5xx responses and retry storms for short windows across affected routes. Impact: generation latency spikes and intermittent request failures for customers pinned to those regions.

What we are doing now:
- Diverting traffic away from impacted AZs to healthy AZs in the same region where possible.
- Activating cross-region reroutes (APAC -> us-west-2; EU -> us-east-1) for tenants that accept cross-region routing.
- Increasing autoscale buffer on Dedicated pools to absorb bursts.

Immediate customer guidance (action required):
1) If you have a hard region pin, please confirm whether cross-region routing is acceptable for the next 12–24 hours. We'll default to cross-region reroute for customers who do not reply.
2) If you run a Private deployment, signal if you need a maintenance window — we will coordinate a minimal configuration change.

Attached: preliminary reroute playbook (reroute_playbook_v1.pdf). We'll follow up with a post-incident note and a draft postmortem tomorrow.

Apologies for the interruption — we’ll keep updates every 2 hours until stable.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T01:22:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC & EU service disruption — immediate customer notice

On Thu, Feb 18, 2027 at 01:04 AM lauren.bishop@redwood.com wrote:
> We're sending a quick update: between 00:40-01:00 UTC we observed escalating connectivity errors in two cloud regions ...

We have the initial traces: looks like a networking fabric flap from the cloud provider causing AZ-level packet loss which amplified into client retries and queue pressure on our frontends. Marcus, can you start the reroute job and bump the per-host connection limit on the in-region frontends?

I'll draft the internal incident timeline and call out the mitigation steps. Also recommend we proactively offer Acme a one-time credit given impact window ~45m. Thoughts?

-Hannah
Incident Response Lead

From: samantha.jenkins@acme-analytics.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: mike@cloudops.io
Date: 2027-02-18T02:10:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC & EU service disruption — immediate customer notice

Lauren — thanks for the quick update. We are seeing request failures from Tokyo and Frankfurt endpoints; our analytics pipelines saw backpressure in our ingestion cluster at 01:10 UTC. Cross-region is acceptable for the short term but we need to preserve data locality where possible. Please confirm whether session affinity and KV cache will be preserved when you reroute us to us-west-2.

Also: can you share any ETA on when the EU endpoints will be back to normal? We have scheduled runs later this morning and want to avoid double processing.

Thanks,
Samantha Jenkins
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T02:35:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC & EU service disruption — immediate customer notice

Action log: started cross-region reroute for tenants enrolled in the 'cross-region-fallback' policy at 02:18 UTC. For tenants without that policy, we queued a notification (will auto-apply fallback at 02:55 UTC).

Technical details:
- Session affinity: we preserve high-level session tokens but the KV local cache will miss on first requests after reroute. We seed the remote cache with KV snapshots for heavy tenants; Acme is on the seed list.
- Token handling: no token re-signing required.
- Expected latency delta: +80–160ms median for APAC -> us-west-2 reroute.

Attachments uploaded to incident folder: trace-APAC-0218.log; postmortem-draft-20270218.docx (working).

Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: samantha.jenkins@acme-analytics.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T03:47:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC & EU service disruption — immediate customer notice

Samantha — thank you. Confirming the answers and next steps:
1) Session affinity: preserved at the token level. You should see cache misses on up to 2% of requests for the first 10 minutes while remote cache seeding completes; Marcus has already seeded Acme's heavy-keyspace.
2) EU ETA: cloud provider reports partial recovery in eu-west-1 starting ~04:30 UTC; full stability TBD. We'll notify you when we see sustained normal telemetry for 15 minutes.
3) To avoid double processing: please pause scheduled ingestion runs for 30 minutes after we signal 'stable'. We'll send a clear 'resume' notice.

Compensation: given the 45m impact window we will apply a one-time 10% credit to this month's usage invoice for Acme; I'll confirm via billing once the postmortem is finalized.

Attached is the customer-facing reroute checklist (reroute_playbook_v1.pdf). If you'd like, we can schedule a 15-minute sync to walk through the precise resume timing.

—Lauren
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-19T09:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: draft postmortem & customer comms checklist

Team —

Thanks for the fast coordination overnight. Attached is the draft postmortem and a small set of follow-up items for the CS/Sales/Engineering teams: postmortem-draft-20270218.docx. Key action items:
- Root cause blameless write-up (owner: Hannah) — 48h
- Provider escalation notes and timeline (owner: Jonas) — 24h
- Customer credits & billing note (owner: Stephanie) — 48h; confirm on Acme credit formally
- Permanent mitigations: add additional cross-region warm pools and improve front-end backpressure handling (owner: Marcus) — roadmap story by EOW

Please review and add comments in the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/incident-20270218-postmortem. I will consolidate and publish the external postmortem draft to impacted customers by EOD tomorrow.

Lauren
Head of Customer Reliability
